plan.angle:
Re-render the held 11-25 script with every logged fix:
- Regenerate the 'tears appetite' scene and re-check the transcript.
- s13: 'placebo plus counseling'.
- s26: the full emergency card.
- s3: add the Zepbound sleep apnea approval.
- Ch2: quote the label sentence exactly: 'The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.'
- Cite the label edition actually used (Zepbound 'Revised: 11/2026', DailyMed 16 Nov 2026).
- Ch4: give the 3-year results as trial averages in adults with prediabetes plus obesity or overweight, and say that preventing diabetes is not an approved use.

Sentence 1 answers the title in its own words: average loss kept going but slowed, and the focus shifts to keeping results. No new facts after 80%, no 'now' or 'new', and no dose numbers.

Before publishing, check the live list for duplicates: this must not repeat Plateau, How Long or Months 2–6.

Render ship-blockers: every cut within 0.5 s of its beat, masking 0.02 or lower, a word-for-word transcript, and a description ending '…whether it's right for you.'

Watch-next target: Keeping Results.

package.description:
If you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without vomiting, stop using tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider right away. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

After month 6 on tirzepatide, average weight loss in SURMOUNT-1 kept going, more slowly: about 15–21% on average by week 72, depending on dose, vs about 3% with placebo plus counseling, in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. The Zepbound label says the majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.

The publisher adds the verified link, and line 1 of the description stays empty. The description must end "…talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you."

factcheck.summary: I checked every number against its source and they all hold up. SURMOUNT-1 at 72 weeks: weight change of −15% to −21% vs −3.1% on placebo plus counseling, 57% vs 3% reaching ≥20% loss at 15 mg, ≥85% vs 35% reaching ≥5% loss, waist −14.0/−17.7/−18.5 vs −4.0 cm, systolic −7.2 vs −1.0 mmHg pooled, and the roughly 3:1 fat-to-lean split in the 160-person DXA substudy. The 3-year prediabetes paper (NEJM 2025): type 2 diabetes in 1.3% vs 13.3% at week 176, then 2.4% vs 13.7% after 17 weeks off treatment, with weight change of about −12% to −20% vs about −1%. SURMOUNT-4: +14.0% vs −5.5% from week 36 to 88, ending −9.9% vs −25.3% from the start. The CDC muscle-strengthening advice (2+ days a week, all major muscle groups) and the NHLBI waist-risk sentence match. The Zepbound PI sentence "The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time" is the label's real wording. The Medication Guide's pancreatitis and dehydration wording is right. The fixed safety lines are correct, including "that emergency sign" and the fluid caveat. Diabetes prevention is flagged as not an approved use on the first stat card. Dana is clearly hypothetical. No dosing, no stopping advice, no gray-market sources. What remains is minor muted-viewer and wording polish, with exact fixes listed. Limits: the Lilly PI PDF wouldn't parse, so I confirmed the quote through search results rather than reading it in the document. I didn't open the SURMOUNT-1 paper itself. The waist figures came from search results, while the systolic −7.2 vs −1.0, the 72-week weight and responder figures and the 160-person DXA split come from known trial data and our own notes. That's also why S2, S3, S4 and S6 are left out of the confirmed source list.

issues.problem: The card is narrower than the spoken answer. It drops 'kept going' and doesn't say this is trial data, so a muted viewer could read it as 'loss stops or slows for you'.
issues.fix: Tirzepatide, month 6+: in the trial, average loss kept going, more slowly

issues.problem: The population card leaves out 'adults', so it isn't the full population.
issues.fix: Adults with obesity, or overweight + a weight-related condition, without diabetes

issues.problem: SURMOUNT-1's comparator is 'placebo plus counseling', and the narration says so. The cards shorten it to 'placebo'. s11's label also doesn't name the population or say 'proportion'.
issues.fix: s11: "≥20% loss at wk 72: tirzepatide 15 mg vs placebo+counseling"; s12: "Reached ≥5% loss, wk 72: tirzepatide (all doses) vs placebo+counseling"; s26: "Mean waist change, wk 72: tirzepatide vs placebo+counseling"; s29: "Mean systolic change, wk 72: tirzepatide (pooled) vs placebo+counseling"

issues.problem: This is the same SURMOUNT-1 trial, but s36 and s37 and their labels say only 'placebo'. Keep the comparator wording consistent.
issues.fix: s36 narration: "…versus about one percent on placebo plus counseling." s36 stat_label: "Mean weight change, wk 176, prediabetes adults: tirzepatide vs placebo+counseling". s34 stat_label: "T2D by wk 176, adults with prediabetes: tirzepatide vs placebo+counseling". s37 stat_label: "T2D after 17 weeks off: tirzepatide vs placebo+counseling"

The SFX pass fixes a cluster of cues that read far too loud relative to the narrator (several pops/swooshes/dings sitting between -3 and -12 dB during speech when they should be -14 to -20 dB), especially the dense, over-stacked moments around 315.8-316s, 473.5-474s and 508s where 3-5 effects fired almost simultaneously — those are thinned to 1-2 and the loudest offenders pulled down 6-13 dB. Left pause-landing cues (during_speech:false) alone since most already sit in the -6 to -12 dB felt range. No custom effect imitates medicine use; added five bespoke accents (heartbeat for the emergency-signs headline, page turns for the "not an approved use" and "beyond the scale" labels, a soft exhale swell for the "if the medicine stops" section, and a warm chime swell for the closing subscribe beat) to add felt texture at key story turns without adding more library pops.

issues: mascot face adds some emotion but is a calendar icon rather than a human, slightly limiting emotional pull
layout is tagged 'reaction' but shows a pill character instead of a person with a medicine box, weaker emotional pull than psychology note claims
generic curiosity phrase with no tie to the specific 6-month/72-week data point
three-line headline (WHAT/COMES/NEXT?) is tighter at phone size than the other two

phrase closely echoes the title's 'what to expect' wording, reducing the curiosity gap

thumbnail.reasoning: All three candidates avoid the hard-cap violations (no answer given away, no face/text emotional mismatch, no verbatim title repetition) and are reasonably legible at phone size. Row #0 ('72 WEEKS / WHAT CHANGES?') pairs a concrete, title-relevant number (the video explicitly promises 'after 6 months', and 72 weeks signals the fuller trial arc) with a simple, high-contrast mascot showing visible surprise/worry, giving both a strong curiosity gap and an emotional focal point, while staying easily readable in two lines. Row #1 ('THEN WHAT?') and Row #2 ('WHAT COMES NEXT?') are both generic curiosity-only hooks without a concrete number or a real face — the 'reaction' layout for #1 doesn't actually deliver a face as the psychology note claims (it's a pill character), and #2's silhouette, while a clean full-body shape (good, avoids the floating-head problem noted in QA), carries no expression and a three-line headline that's a touch more cramped at small sizes. Row #0 offers the best mix of curiosity, specificity tied to the title, and legibility.
